evidence: Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml lines 5-8 (floor at lines 10-11) read '[weights] functional = 0.6 / polish = 0.2 / visual = 0.2', byte-identical to the frozen template scoring.toml (diff clean) and to the SKILL.md delivery profile ('Reward is shaped - functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2'). Gates are 0.0 and carry no mass; score.py computes the reward only from [weights]. Maximum contribution of the non-functional dimensions is 0.40, below functional's 0.60, as the row's sanity check asks. Per-criterion weights (parsed, not estimated): functional has 43 binary criteria totalling 59.0 with weights 1.0 (17 criteria), 1.5 (20) and 2.0 (6); polish has 6 binary criteria all 1.0; visual has 3 likert criteria all 1.0. The six 2.0 criteria are the deepest multi-rule outcomes that the brief itself stresses ('paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it', 'without losing a draft when another tab saves first'): cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic, cw_same_line_carets, cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo, cw_last_good_recovery, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state. The 1.0 tier holds the simpler single-outcome checks (cw_custom_typing_and_line_join, cw_basic_run_output, cw_console_levels_in_order, cw_html_preview, cw_replace_current). Functional mass by area: run/preview/console lifecycle 16.5, saved-record persistence and multi-tab concurrency 11.5, core editing 10.5, multi-caret 5.5, find/replace 5.0, formatting 4.5, preview isolation and dynamic-code refusal 3.0, syntax colouring 2.5 (sum 59.0). The only presentation-leaning functional area, colouring, is the lightest at 4.2 percent of functional; no structural or DOM-shape criterion sits in the scored suites (the DOM-surface check is a zero-weight gate). Ranking attempt with the shipped policy: an app that barely clears the floor (3.0/59 = 0.0508 > 0.05) with perfect polish and visual scores 0.6*0.0508 + 0.4 = 0.43, while a fully functional app with zero polish and the lowest visual ratings still scores at least 0.60, so style cannot outrank function at the extremes. NOTES (not defects). (1) Per-criterion reward mass is uneven across dimensions because the fixed 0.2 dimension weights are divided among few criteria: each visual likert criterion carries 0.2/3 = 6.67 percent of the reward and each polish criterion 0.2/6 = 3.33 percent, against 1.02 / 1.53 / 2.03 percent for a functional criterion of weight 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0. So cw_visual_component_finish alone is worth more than cw_preview_isolation (1.53 percent) and cw_last_good_recovery (2.03 percent) together. This follows from the template-mandated 0.6/0.2/0.2 split and a large functional suite; the template itself ships 6 visual and 4 polish criteria, so this task concentrates visual mass more than the template does, but the dimension totals are unchanged and the task may not alter them. A mid-range consequence: an app at 50 percent functional with perfect polish/visual (0.70) outscores an app at 80 percent functional with half polish and weak visual (about 0.48 + 0.10 + 0.04-0.08), which is a property of the shared policy rather than of this task's weights. (2) cw_js_semantic_coloring is weighted 1.5 while cw_basic_run_output is 1.0; the colouring criterion demands five distinct categories plus declaration/call consistency and so proves a real tokenizer, and a working Run is separately a precondition of roughly seventeen other functional criteria, so core execution is not under-weighted in effect. (3) Three polish criteria (cw_focus_returns_to_code, cw_undo_redo_availability, cw_unsaved_marker) are behavioural rather than stylistic, which makes the 0.2 polish mass more functional, not less honest. Runtime evidence: no configured judge run exists for these bytes; the hosted run in the evidence index is of an earlier candidate (41 functional criteria then, 43 now) and is not used as a measurement here. This row is decidable from the static weight tables, so no required measurement is missing.
